summary:
VISUAL QA, ROUND 3: not a pass. 3 blockers, all ui, all small. All 7 round 2 blockers are fixed, and the signup and billing screens are now at the bar in both themes at 1440, 768 and 390. What is left is one typographic bug on the verify screen, one console error in the WMS, and a short polish list.

**What I did**
- Built 16 fresh accounts through the real screens with the test gateway, one per billing state.
- Took 726 screenshots in light and dark at 1440, 768 and 390 against the shared dev servers, and looked at them as contact sheets and crops.
- Ran script checks on every capture for sideways scroll, small tap targets and console errors, plus a sweep at 320 and 360 wide.
- Measured text contrast on 20 pages in both themes, input focus rings, busy states on a slow network, and reduced motion.
- Clicked the create buttons in view only and locked apps, the seat offer, the warehouse limit offer and the company step.
- Did not restart any server; all six are still up and the working tree is unchanged.

**Round 2 blockers, rechecked**
- **Focus on text fields:** fixed. The focused border measures 18.1 to 1 in light and 15.6 to 1 in dark. Off switches now show a clear grey track (seen, not measured).
- **View only WMS and Pulse:** fixed. "Add client", "Create client" and "Bulk import/update" in the WMS open the view only dialog and are dimmed. So do the Pulse labor, jobs and welcome pages.
- **Locked Projects:** fixed. All four apps use one lock frame with no create buttons.
- **WMS first screen:** fixed. Only the name is needed, the rest is filled in, the short code is explained, and "Back to Portal" is there.
- **404:** fixed. Themed page with two ways on, signed in and signed out.
- **Organization page on phones:** fixed. Names and emails wrap, with controls on a second line.
- **Polish list:** fixed. The picker shows one unit when yearly, launcher tiles say "Update your card", Pulse `/jobs/new` keeps the app frame, and the seat offer has one filled button.

**What else passed**
- No sideways scroll from 320 to 1440 on any page checked.
- No text below 4.5 to 1.
- Busy state within 120 ms on signup, picker and pay.
- Confetti stops under reduced motion.
- Banners and lock screens use the same words and button in the Portal, CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse.
- The marketing pricing page, wizard handoff and email templates look right.

**Why it fails**
1. The verify email screen starts a line with a stray period.
2. The view only WMS dashboard throws a hydration error on most loads.
3. A short polish list: the warehouse offer looks like an error, the phone guide count is wrong, one tap target is small, and two smaller items.

**Seen, not blockers**
- The WMS kept showing "Free trial. 9 days left" for at least 40 seconds after I ended the trial with the test tool. The integrator disclosed this gap earlier.
- CRM and WMS setup guide rows squeeze their titles on phones ("Create your …"). That is the apps' own guide, not a billing screen.
- The test invoice shows "localhost:3600" under the seller name, until `BILLING_SELLER_ADDRESS` is set.

**Not checked**
- Real Stripe pages and the Google and Microsoft buttons (no keys).
- The "billing is off" production state (the port 3310 build is stopped).
- Loading skeletons (I could not trigger them on the dev server).
- Projects in view only.

Everything is in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/visual3/` (`shots/`, `sheets/`, `audit-*.json`, `scripts/`, `notes.txt`). The `x*` files are the interaction checks.

blockers.title: Verify email screen starts a line with a stray period
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/components/ui/email-text.tsx (the inline-block span) and apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/verify-email/verify-email-form.tsx line 187; the invite screens use the same component
blockers.detail:
Wrong: the sentence under "Check your email" breaks as "We sent a 6 digit code to maya@northwind.example" and then a new line that begins ". It works for 10 minutes."
- It happens at 1440 with the spec's own sample address, maya@northwind.example.

Reproduce: sign up with maya@northwind.example on a desktop and look at /verify-email. See shots/x92-verify-short-email--desktop-light.png and shots/a30-verify--desktop-light.png, --tablet-dark and --phone-light.
Great looks like: the period always stays attached to the address. Either keep the address inline with its break points, or end the first sentence before the address and put the address on its own line. Check the invite screens that use the same component.

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. 7 blockers (4 backend, 3 ui). None is a fake charge, a double charge or an access leak. They are wrong words or wrong states at the edges of the money flow: cancel while a payment is late, email links for signed out people, a late retry email, the bundle discount ending, a stale app banner, and the new billing only role.

**How I tested**
- Drove the real product with Playwright and signed webhook calls on the shared dev stack, test gateway on, plan gate on (`ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0`).
- Made 5 new organizations and 5 invited people. Read `core.entitlements`, `billing_subscriptions`, `billing_invoices`, `billing_events`, `billing_emails` and the audit log after each step.
- No product code edited. Scripts, outputs and screenshots: `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/opqa3/`.
- The Portal dev server was killed for lack of memory once (5.1 GB). I restarted it with `ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0 deploy/dev/app-start.sh portal`. All six are up and the working tree is clean.

**Round 2 blockers, rechecked: all 6 of mine are fixed**
- Out of order and repeated invoice events add no false activity lines (5 invoices, 5 payment lines, 0 failures).
- A stale confirm now keeps the other person's change and says so.
- The yearly switch sentence adds up, and credit lines name the full days.
- A decline on the invite seat offer shows inside the offer with "Update card", and keeps the email.
- WMS first run: no console errors, and one click creates the warehouse.
- Card 0341 pays a plan change and fails the next renewal, also when saved on the card page.
- Security fixes hold from the customer side: two checkouts raced gave one plan and one invoice, the same change confirmed in two tabs gave one invoice, and a stale tab after an organization switch is refused with "You switched organizations. Reload this page."

**What works, with real results**
- Wizard to signup: bad inputs, weak password, duplicate email, back, forward, refresh and a double click all hold. Signup to picker took 1.5 s.
- Trial: rows are source trial, 14 days out. Reminder emails go at 7, 3 and 1 days and at the end. Apps add and remove from the lock screens.
- Checkout: declined, no funds and 3DS fail write no rows. 3DS approve and TEST10 work, and $355.68 matches on checkout, success, billing home and the invoice.
- Changes: seats, warehouses, apps, monthly to yearly and back, and yearly seat changes all matched their invoices to the cent. A yearly renewal used the credit.
- Failed payment: past due, retries, last day email, view only on day 7, the gateway closing the plan, recovery by card in 2.9 s, and paying again with no second trial.
- Cancel, keep, end, reactivate, and pause, undo, start again all work.
- Roles: a member and an admin are refused on pages and on replayed server actions. A billing manager and a billing only invite work and use no seat.
- Two orgs for one user: switching works and the other org's invoice gives "We could not find that."

**Not verified**
- Real Stripe, real email, Google and Microsoft sign in.
- Production with no keys (I did not rebuild; the integrator's run covers it).
- "Your bank needs to approve" at a renewal: the test gateway always passes that card off session, so that email and "Pay now" path cannot be reached from the UI.

blockers.title: Cancel while a payment is late gives wrong words, hides the cancel, and can still charge
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/cancel.ts and packages/billing/src/plan-state.ts (phase when cancel is set and a payment is late); apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/cancel/page.tsx line 73; apps/portal/src/features/billing/phase-copy.ts; billing home flash 'canceled'
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: a paid plan whose renewal fails (card 4000 0000 0000 0341, skip 30 days), then skip 8 days so the apps are view only. Billing home offers "Cancel plan".

What is wrong:
1. The cancel page says "Your plan will end on Dec 16, 2026. You keep everything until then." The banner right above it says the apps are view only now. Both cannot be true.
2. After "Cancel my plan" the flash says "Your plan is set to end. You keep everything until then." Billing home then shows no end date and no "Keep my plan". It still says "We will try $348.80 again" and offers "Cancel plan" a second time. DB: status past_due, cancel_at_period_end true, invoice still open.
3. The retries keep running on a plan the customer just canceled. Saving a new card charged $348.80 at once. The card page only says "If a payment is due, we try it right after you save."
4. The same happens on day 0 of a late payment by opening /billing/cancel.

Script: docs/billing/.review/opqa3/32-cardpage.js and 33-cancel-unpaid.js. Screenshot: shots/c-unpaid-cancel.png.

What great looks like: pick one honest rule and say it. Either a cancel with a bill open ends the plan now and voids that bill ("Your plan ends today. We will not charge the $348.80."), or the page says "You still owe $348.80 for Nov 16 to Dec 16. Pay it to keep full access until Dec 16." Billing home shows the cancel with "Keep my plan" in every phase, never a second "Cancel plan". Add a test for cancel in past_due and in unpaid.

blockers.title: Signed out links lose where they were going: every email button lands on the launcher
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx line 19 (requirePageSession('/')); apps/portal/src/server/session.ts; apps/portal/src/server/billing/context.ts requireBillingContext
blockers.detail:
Reproduce, signed out:
- curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' 'http://localhost:3300/billing?fix=payment' gives /login?next=%2F.
- The same for /billing/plan?add=projects, /billing/invoices and /settings/organization.
- Sign in and you land on / (the launcher), not on the page you asked for.

Why: the (app) layout runs first and always redirects with next=/. The page level return paths in requireBillingContext('/billing/...') never get used, and they would drop the query (fix=payment, add=, from=) anyway.

Why it matters: the one button in the failed payment email ("Update card", /billing?fix=payment), "Pick a plan" in the trial emails and "View invoice" in receipts all open the launcher for anyone whose session has ended. That is the person those emails are for. The owner then has to find Billing and the card button alone.

What great looks like: the login redirect carries the full path and query that was asked for (safeNextPath already guards it), and sign in returns there. Add an e2e: signed out, open /billing?fix=payment, sign in, land on billing with "Update card" in focus.

blockers.title: A retry that fails after day 7 sends an email with dates that have already passed
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/emails/templates/payment.ts paymentFailed (lines 72 to 100) and the payload built for invoice.payment_failed
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: let a renewal fail with card 0341 and keep skipping days. The third try runs on day 8, one day after the apps became view only.

The email for that try reads: "We try again on: Dec 1, 2026. Full access until: Nov 23, 2026. Update your card by Nov 23, 2026 to keep full access." It was written on Nov 24. The payload shows attempt 4, accessChangesAt 2026-11-23, nextRetryAt 2026-12-01. It tells the customer to act by yesterday to keep access they have already lost.

The template has no branch for a date in the past. Stripe retries often run for two to three weeks, so every late retry sends this.

A second, smaller case in the same file: when the gateway gives up, the "Your plan has ended" email, billing home and the activity line do not say why. A customer who never canceled reads "Your plan ended on Nov 23" with no reason.

What great looks like:
- After the access date the email says "Your apps are view only now. Pay $164.00 to turn them back on." with the next retry date and no "keep full access" line.
- The plan ended email and the home line say "We could not collect $164.00 after 4 tries, so your plan ended."
- A render test covers accessChangesAt in the past.

blockers.title: Removing an app can raise the bill, and the confirm screen does not say so
blockers.where: Change preview words in packages/billing/src (changes and plan-state copy for removals that end the bundle discount); PlanPicker change mode and the confirm panel on /billing/plan
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: a plan with CRM (7 seats) and Pulse, monthly, $185.60. On /billing/plan turn Pulse off and press Review change.

The panel says: "Remove Pulse. Due today $12.77. $148.87 for the 22 days left in this period. Less $136.10 for what you take off. Then $203.00 per month."

So taking an app off costs $12.77 today and $17.40 more every month, because the 20% bundle discount ends. Nothing in the title, the sentence or the picker says that. The only hint is "Add a second app and save 20% on both." A person removing an app to save money pays more and cannot tell why. Screenshot: docs/billing/.review/opqa3/shots/d-preview-bundle-lost.png.

Related wording on a credit: removing WMS and Pulse says "That is $195.25 for the 14 full days left of what you take off, less $67.67 for what you add." Nothing was added. The $67.67 is CRM going back to full price.

Billing home already does this well the other way ("Adds the bundle discount. You pay $5.80 less per month.").

What great looks like:
- A plain warning before confirm: "Removing Pulse ends your 20% bundle discount. Your plan goes from $185.60 to $203.00 per month. Keeping Pulse costs less."
- The math sentence names the cause: "CRM goes back to full price for the 22 days left: $148.87. Less $136.10 for the time you did not use."
- Never "for what you add" when nothing is added.

blockers.title: App banners stay wrong for about a minute after good news
blockers.where: packages/entitlements/src/read.ts (60 second cache per process, CACHE_TTL_MS); the plan banner in CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse; SPEC 8.4
blockers.detail:
Measured in real time, no test tools (docs/billing/.review/opqa3/43-lag.js):
- Cancel the plan in the Portal. CRM showed no banner for 64 seconds and Pulse for 40 seconds.
- Press "Keep my plan". CRM kept showing "Your plan ends on Dec 24. You keep everything until then. Keep my plan" for 64 seconds. Pulse kept it for 40 seconds.

The owner undoes the cancel, goes back to the CRM, and is told the plan is still ending, with a "Keep my plan" button for something already done. The same lag shows after paying again when a plan had ended: the CRM still said "Your plan ends on Dec 24" on an active plan.

SPEC 8.4 says: "After a write, the entitlement cache is cleared, and the other apps see good news on their next request." That holds only when the old state was not full access. Changes between two full access states (cancel set and undone, pause set and undone, payment fixed inside the 7 days) are served stale by each app's own cache.

What great looks like: the apps read a cheap version stamp for the organization (bumped on every billing write) before they trust the cached answer, or links back from the Portal carry a fresh marker. The banner is right on the first page load after any change. Add a test: keep the plan, open the CRM at once, no banner.

blockers.title: A billing only person is offered apps they cannot open, and the apps show a 404 or a login form
blockers.where: Portal header 'Switch app' menu and 'Apps' nav for the billing role (apps/portal/src/features/shell); CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse entry for a member with the billing only role
blockers.detail:
The new "Invite someone for billing only" works well in the Portal: it is free, uses no seat, lands on Billing and can change the plan.

But the header still shows:
- "Switch app", which lists "KitStak CRM, Active" and "KitStak WMS, Active" as normal links.
- "Apps", which only bounces back to /billing.

Reproduce as the invited bookkeeper:
- Open CRM from the menu: "This page doesn't exist. Check the address, or head back to your workspace." with a 404 console error.
- Open WMS from the menu: the WMS "Log in" form, though the person is signed in.

Both are dead ends that look like a broken product. Screenshot: docs/billing/.review/opqa3/shots/bk-app.png. Script: 60-misc.js and 65-reactivate-b.js.

What great looks like:
- For this role the app menu shows only the Portal, or shows the apps as "Billing only. Ask an owner for access."
- The "Apps" tab is hidden.
- Each app shows the shared lock frame with "You manage billing for OPQA C. You do not have a seat in the apps. Back to Billing." No 404, no login form, no console error.

blockers.title: Small wrong turns on real paths
blockers.where: Portal /billing flash after a card fix (apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/page.tsx); /settings/organization member rows and invite form (member-rows.tsx, invite-member-form.tsx)
blockers.detail:
Each is small. Together they are the gap to the best products.

1. No way back after fixing a payment from an app. The CRM banner link is /billing?fix=payment&from=crm. After the card is saved the flash says "Card updated. Your payment went through." with no "Back to CRM" link. Adding an app from a lock screen does give "Back to Projects". The "Update card" link in the invite seat offer also does not return to the invite.

2. "Remove" on a member acts on one click. There is no confirm, no message after, and no undo. The person loses access at once (their next page is "Create your organization"). Great looks like a short confirm that names the person and says what happens to the seat: "Remove Drew Patel? They lose access now. You still pay for 5 seats until you lower them."

3. Inviting someone who is already in the team shows the raw message "User is already a member of this organization", with no full stop and not in our words. Great looks like "Sam is already on your team."

4. A plain member sees setup guide steps they cannot do ("Tell us about your business" with no button).

Reproduce: docs/billing/.review/opqa3/31-recover.js, 63-members.js, 10-team.js.

blockers.title: An admin can make themselves (or anyone) a billing manager through the shared sign in API, so the owner only rule is not enforced
blockers.detail:
SPEC P15 says only an owner can add or remove a billing manager, and that admins can see billing but not pay, change or cancel. The Portal action `inviteBillingManagerAction` checks this, but the role itself is granted by the role name `billing` in `core.member.role`, and nothing guards that name at the shared Better Auth organization endpoints.

Reproduced on the running dev portal (port 3300) with a throwaway owner and a plain admin in one organization:
1. Signed in as the ADMIN: `POST /api/auth/organization/update-member-role` with `{memberId: <own member id>, role: ["admin","billing"], organizationId}` answered 200. The database row then read `admin,billing`.
2. Signed in as the ADMIN: `POST /api/auth/organization/invite-member` with `{email: <outside address>, role: "billing"}` answered 200 and made a pending billing invite.
3. `/billing/team` then listed the admin under "People who can manage billing" with kind `manager`, and listed the outside invite.

By code, `billingAccessFor` sets `canManage` for any role string that holds `billing`, so that admin can now change the plan (which charges the card on file), cancel, pause, edit the billing email and details, and open the card update page. The same endpoints are mounted by the CRM and the other apps, so the door is open at each of them. The admin can also give the role to any other member the same way.

Great looks like: the rule lives in `billingOrganizationOptions` so it holds at every door. `beforeCreateInvitation`, `beforeUpdateMemberRole` and `beforeAddMember` refuse, with one plain sentence ("Only an owner can add or remove a billing manager."), any change that adds or removes the `billing` role unless the acting person is an active owner of that organization. Add a test per hook (admin refused, owner allowed, nothing written on refusal) and one e2e call as an admin against the real endpoint. The commands I ran by hand are saved in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec3/admin-billing-role.sh (not run again as a script, because the sign up rate limit was reached).
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts (organizationHooks: beforeCreateInvitation, beforeUpdateMemberRole, beforeAddMember), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/access.ts (billingAccessFor), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/auth/src/access-control.ts (the `billing` role), endpoints /api/auth/organization/update-member-role and /api/auth/organization/invite-member

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. One backend blocker, reproduced on the running dev portal. The three round 2 blockers are fixed and I confirmed each by running code.

**What I ran**
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/billing`: 26 files, 484 tests pass, with the database up. `packages/entitlements`: 44 pass.
- The round 2 probe scripts again, unchanged, against the current code (`docs/billing/.review/sec2/`).
- curl against the dev portal with throwaway accounts and one throwaway organization. I removed them afterwards (0 users, 0 organizations, 0 activity rows left). No shared server was restarted. The working tree is clean.
- I did not rerun the Playwright suite or a production build, and nobody has run real Stripe.

**Round 2 blockers, rechecked**
- **Two checkouts at once:** 12 tries of the race made one gateway customer every time, and the older pay page was closed. Paying the closed page answers "This checkout page has closed".
- **Same plan change confirmed three times at once:** one $96.67 invoice, one `plan.changed` line, one receipt. A stale basis and a wrong amount both answer `price_changed`.
- **Stale tab:** every billing action now takes the organization the page was made for and refuses with `org_changed` when it differs (read in code, with a unit test and `stale-tab.spec.ts`).

**Also checked and sound**
- Webhooks are verified on the raw body before anything is read. The ledger claim and the state change commit together. The test webhook route answers 404 outside test gateway mode.
- No price or amount comes from the browser. The catalog cents are exact (yearly and bundle amounts checked by hand). Eight upgrade and downgrade cycles never gave the customer a net gain.
- An unpaid checkout session grants nothing. Another organization's session answers `not_found`.
- Test gateway pages, test actions and `/dev/outbox` are closed in production by a request time check.
- Redirect helpers accept only same origin paths. Return paths are glued to app origins from env.
- No secret in the diff, and no `.env` file is tracked.
- Better Auth refuses to link a Google sign in to a local account whose email is not verified, and refuses to list invites for an unverified email.
- Email templates escape every value. The activity CSV guards formula cells.
- Migrations 0007 to 0009 are additive and safe to run again.

**Not blockers, but worth fixing**
1. **Real Stripe is still unrun.** Pending updates on a period change, proration dates in the future and invoice previews have never met the real API. This is the largest open risk.
2. **Database tests still skip silently** when Postgres is not reachable, and the repo has no CI file. Add a switch that makes them fail.
3. **Webhook handlers hold a database connection and the organization lock across several gateway calls.** A burst of events can starve a small pool.
4. **The billing turn lease is 120 seconds**, but the Stripe SDK can wait longer than that across retries, so a slow Stripe could let a second step start.
5. **Reset codes:** about 100 guesses a day per address on a 6 digit code. Consider a longer code or a lock after several used up codes.
6. **`changeUnverifiedEmailAction` deletes codes with `LIKE '%old email'`.** It can remove other people's pending codes when their address ends the same way, and `_` in an address is a wildcard. Match the exact identifiers instead.
7. **CRM invites made through its own `/api/v1/invitations` route send no email.** The CRM dialog honestly says to copy the link, but SPEC 5.5 says every invite sends an email, and the CRM onboarding screen says "invitations sent".
8. **A trial overwrites a row staff revoked by hand**, though `read.ts` says a manual revoke stays a lock.
9. **One trial per person is still check then write** (parallel trials, no extra days).
10. **Test gateway actions check membership only**, not billing rights (test mode only).
11. **Failed query text, with its values, can land in `core.billing_events.error` and the log** (capped at 500 characters).
12. **For the owner:** the 20% bundle discount applies to every app, so a team with 13 or more CRM seats pays less by adding Pulse than by not adding it. This follows the decided catalog. I flag it only so it is a choice.

Not passed. Scorecard 23 of 30 with no zero (bar is 24; round 1 was 20, round 2 was 22). Full head to head is in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/reviews/critic-round-3.md; scripts and screenshots are in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/critic3/ (not committed). I used real Chromium against the shared dev stack with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0 on every server (checked per process), did not edit product code, did not restart servers, and ran deploy/dev/rate-limit-reset.sh once.

Three people tested: Dana (CRM + WMS, desktop, light and dark, full life cycle), Jo (Pulse only, 360 px phone, dark, trial end with no card, then pay), Priya (billing only bookkeeper invite).

Nine of the eleven round 2 blockers are closed and closed well: yearly switch sentence is right and adds up; the day rule for seats is stated on the dialog and pricing page; the WMS opens in one click with everything filled in; the launcher puts my apps first (Open Pulse at 245 px on a 360 px phone); "Pick a plan" to a card field is 2 clicks and 0 fields; guest role, several invites at once and a seat cost line all work, and over the limit it sends what fits and asks before adding seats; the signup page now has a real screenshot, prices or my cart and three true promises; a bookkeeper can join free by email. Measured: account made in 0.8 s, trial started in 0.8 s, 4 fields and 5 clicks from the home page to the launcher, Pulse fully open 2.5 s after paying on an ended trial. Billing (price math, invoices, failed payment, cancel, invites) is the best I have used.

What still keeps it from a pass: real Stripe has still never run; the signup page has no Google, Microsoft or email code door on screen; "Remove WMS" explains its credit with "less $106.33 for what you add" when nothing is added (it is the bundle discount ending) and nothing warns that the CRM price per user rises from $23.20 to $29; the new 15 character rule accepts passwordpassword, aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa and 123456789012345 on the server and the meter calls them Good while ticking rules the password does not meet; the billing only person is asked for a 6 digit code after arriving from her invite email and is shown a setup step that dead ends in the CRM; the sign in side panel sells trial prices on login, reset, verify and invite pages; plus a short list of small contradictions.

Not verified: real Stripe (no keys), Google and Microsoft sign in (no keys). Competitor facts come from COMPETITORS.md working knowledge. Waiting on the owner: Stripe and social test keys, BILLING_SELLER_ADDRESS, BILLING_SUPPORT_REPLY_TIME, and a decision on whether CRM, WMS and Projects prices are confirmed (PRICING_IS_PLACEHOLDER is false per DECISIONS.md section 1, while this review's brief says only Pulse is confirmed). Downgraded from round 2, not a blocker: apps lag the Portal by about a minute after a trial ends or a payment fails; harmless in real time.

blockers.title: Real Stripe has never been run end to end
blockers.where: packages/billing Stripe adapter, stripe:setup, /api/billing/webhooks/stripe, docs/billing/GO-LIVE.md Open item 1
blockers.detail: Unchanged from rounds 1 and 2. Every payment in three reviews and the e2e suite used the test gateway. Hosted Checkout, wallets, Billing Portal card update, live signed webhooks, Stripe's invoice PDF and the future proration date are unseen. Great: the one hour run in GO-LIVE.md Open item 1, recorded, in Stripe test mode, every line pass (stripe:setup check all ok; working, declined and bank approval cards; a promo code; a card update; a replayed webhook; three carts where Stripe's total equals our quote to the cent). This needs sk_test and whsec values from the owner; the team cannot close it alone, so ask the owner for the keys in one line.

blockers.title: Signup has one door and it needs a password: no Google, Microsoft or email code on screen
blockers.where: Portal /signup and /login; apps/portal/src/features/signup/social.ts; code flow in apps/portal/src/server/auth.ts
blockers.detail: Saw: no 'Continue with Google', no 'Continue with Microsoft', no 'Email me a code instead'. Social buttons exist in code and hide with no keys (right rule) but nobody has ever seen them work. Linear, Notion, Slack, HubSpot, Shopify and Vercel all show a Google button on the first screen. Fixers reported 'Email me a code instead' was not built. Great, either is enough: (a) a link under the password field 'Email me a code instead' that uses the existing 6 digit code so the code is both sign in and verification; or (b) a recorded run with Google and Microsoft test client keys showing both buttons on /signup and /login, a new account made with each, and the same person signing in again.

blockers.title: Removing an app gives the wrong reason for its credit
blockers.where: packages/billing change-words (creditNote), shown in the confirm dialog on /billing/plan
blockers.detail: Repro: paid plan with CRM 5 users + WMS 1 warehouse, monthly, mid period. Switch WMS off, Review change. Dialog says: 'You get $183.49 credit on your next bill. That is $289.82 for the 22 full days left of what you take off, less $106.33 for what you add.' The buyer adds nothing. The $106.33 is the CRM going back to list price because the 20% bundle discount needs two apps. 'See the math' shows 'KitStak CRM (5 users) for the 22 days left in this period $106.33' with no reason. Numbers are right, the sentence is not. Great: name the discount and make every number add up, for example '$204.75 back for WMS, for the 22 full days left. Your CRM goes from $23.20 to $29 per user, because the bundle discount needs 2 apps. That takes $21.26 off the credit.' Never say 'what you add' when nothing is added. Add unit tests for a change that ends the bundle and one that starts it.

blockers.title: The 15 character password rule accepts passwords every rival refuses
blockers.where: packages/auth/src/password-policy-plugin.ts (passwordIssues, the passphrase branch)
blockers.detail: Saw in code and on /signup: passwordpassword, aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa, 123456789012345 and qwertyuiopasdfgh pass. Past 15 characters only the length and 'not your email name' are checked. Stripe refuses these. Great: keep '15 or more characters is enough by itself', and refuse one character repeated, a short word repeated, straight runs (1234, qwerty), the most common 1,000 passwords and the company name, with one kind line: 'That one is too easy to guess. Try a few words that do not go together.' Tests for each case and for 'correct horse battery staple' passing.

blockers.title: The password meter says things that are not true
blockers.where: Portal /signup, /invite/[id], /reset-password: strength meter and the four rule checklist
blockers.detail: Repro: type 'correct horse battery staple'. The list shows four green ticks: 'A capital and a small letter, done', 'A number, done', 'A symbol, done'. None is in the password (screenshot 02-signup-passphrase.png). Type passwordpassword or 123456789012345: the meter says 'Good'. danadanadanadana with email dana@... shows no warning until submit. Great: when the long rule is met the four short rules fold away or read 'Not needed' and one green line stays: '15 or more characters. That is enough.' The meter never says Good or Strong for a repeated, run or common password or one the server would refuse. The email name rule shows as I type.

blockers.title: Billing only person is asked for a 6 digit code right after opening her invite email
blockers.where: Invite accept for every role (/invite/[id]); verified email rule in packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts; core.user.email_verified
blockers.detail: Repro: owner sends 'Invite someone for billing only' from /billing/team. Open the invite link, set a password, join. She lands in Billing (good), then a blue bar says 'Enter the 6 digit code we emailed you' and /billing/plan is locked with 'Verify your email first'. core.user.email_verified is false. She proved the address by opening the invite, yet gets a second email and a code step before she can do the one job she was invited for. Great: joining through an invite link with the invited address marks it verified, for every role. No second email, no bar. Keep the address locked on that page. Slack and Linear work this way.

blockers.title: Billing only person is shown app setup she cannot do, and it dead ends
blockers.where: Portal /settings/organization (setup guide) and app links for the billing role; CRM not found page at /[org]; invite page side panel
blockers.detail: Repro as the bookkeeper: Organization page shows 'Set up Whitlock Supply Co, 4 of 5 done' with 'Create your CRM workspace, Open CRM'. Click it: the CRM says 'This page doesn't exist. Check the address, or head back to your workspace.' Her invite page shows 'Prices after your 14 free days' for four apps she will never open. Great: a billing only person sees no setup guide and no app links in the Portal. If she reaches an app anyway it says 'You have billing access only. Ask an owner if you need this app.' with 'Back to Billing'. Her invite panel says what she joins: 'Whitlock Supply Co. Billing only. Free. You can pay bills, change the card and download invoices.'

blockers.title: Nothing warns that the bundle discount ends when you drop to one app
blockers.where: Portal /billing/plan change mode ('Your new plan' panel and confirm dialog) and the trial picker /signup/plan
blockers.detail: Repro: with CRM + WMS the panel says 'The bundle discount stays as long as you have 2 or more apps.' Switch WMS off: that line just disappears. The panel shows 'CRM: 5 users x $29 = $145' and nothing says the CRM price per user went from $23.20 to $29 (25% up). Great: the moment the cart drops to one app, a calm line in the panel: 'With 1 app the 20% bundle discount ends. CRM goes from $23.20 to $29 per user.' The confirm dialog repeats it above the amounts.

blockers.title: The side panel on sign in pages sells a trial to people who are not buying
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx and its panel: /login, /forgot-password, /verify-email, /invite/[id]
blockers.detail: Saw: 'Prices after your 14 free days' with the four list prices beside 'Welcome back' on /login, beside 'Reset your password', beside the invite form for a teammate who will never pay, and on /verify-email after I had already picked CRM and WMS (my cart vanished from the panel and list prices came back). On /signup the panel is right. Great: the panel fits the page. /login and /forgot-password: the screenshot and 'One sign in for every KitStak app', no prices. /verify-email: my cart and 'Your free trial ends on Dec 8, 2026.' /invite: the organization, who invited me and my role in plain words.

blockers.title: Small true things that add up
blockers.where: Portal /billing (usage), /welcome, /settings/organization invite form, /signup and /signup/plan on a phone, rate limit message, email field
blockers.detail: (1) Billing home usage reads 'Seats: 1 of 5 used' with the bar one fifth full, then 'Every seat is in use' because 4 invites hold seats. Great: 'Seats: 5 of 5 in use. 1 person and 4 open invites.' with the bar full and the invite part lighter. (2) Welcome wizard last step shows '1 of 5 done' and a green Done for 'Tell us about your business'; leave without pressing 'Looks good' and the launcher says '0 of 5 done' and asks again. Save answers when given, or do not show Done before saving. (3) Over the seat limit the invite form sends the ones that fit and offers seats for the rest, but after a reload the offer and the unsent addresses are gone with no word. Say '2 people were not invited yet: ...' and keep them until I add seats or dismiss. (4) At 360 px the password rule list pushes 'Company or team' and 'Create account' below the first screen; show one line of hint until typing starts. (5) Phone picker for a Pulse only buyer shows CRM and WMS first and Pulse fourth; put chosen apps first as the launcher does. (6) 'Too many tries. Wait a few minutes' should say how long. (7) dana@gmial.com gets no 'Did you mean gmail.com?' hint.
